hints: Calculate the kinetic energy at $P$ and at $Q$ using $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ with $m = 4\text{ kg}$.
Subtract the kinetic energy at $Q$ from that at $P$: $\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}(4)(12^2 - 8^2)$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the decrease in kinetic energy between $P$ ($v_P = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$) and $Q$ ($v_Q = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$) with mass $m = 4\text{ kg}$:
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}m(v_P^2 - v_Q^2)$$
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}(4)(12^2 - 8^2) = 2(144 - 64) = 2(80) = 160\text{ J}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the formula for kinetic energy:
$$E_k = \frac{1}{2}m v^2$$

Calculate the initial kinetic energy at point $P$ where $v_P = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $m = 4\text{ kg}$:
$$E_{k, P} = \frac{1}{2}(4)(12^2) = 2 \times 144 = 288\text{ J}$$

Calculate the final kinetic energy at point $Q$ where $v_Q = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$E_{k, Q} = \frac{1}{2}(4)(8^2) = 2 \times 64 = 128\text{ J}$$

Calculate the decrease in kinetic energy:
$$\text{Decrease} = E_{k, P} - E_{k, Q} = 288 - 128 = 160\text{ J}$$

hints: Find the gain in potential energy: $mg h = 4(10)(10\sin 30^\circ)$.
Apply the work-energy principle: Work Done by Pushing Force plus Loss in Kinetic Energy equals Gain in Potential Energy.
walkthrough:
Calculate the gravitational potential energy gained moving $10\text{ m}$ up the $30^\circ$ incline with $m = 4\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh = 4(10)(10\sin 30^\circ) = 40(10 \times 0.5) = 200\text{ J}$$

Apply the work-energy principle connecting work done, kinetic energy change, and potential energy gain:
$$W + \text{Decrease in } E_k = \text{Gain in } E_p$$
$$W + 160 = 200$$

Solve for the work done by the pushing force:
$$W = 200 - 160 = 40\text{ J}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Calculate the vertical height gained as the block travels $d = 10\text{ m}$ along the incline:
$$h = d\sin 30^\circ = 10 \times 0.5 = 5\text{ m}$$

Calculate the gain in gravitational potential energy:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh = 4 \times 10 \times 5 = 200\text{ J}$$

State the work-energy theorem for the motion from $P$ to $Q$:
$$\text{Work done by driving force} = \Delta E_p + \Delta E_k$$
Here the kinetic energy decreases by $160\text{ J}$, which helps to overcome gravity:
$$W_{\text{push}} = \Delta E_p - (E_{k, P} - E_{k, Q})$$
$$W_{\text{push}} = 200 - 160 = 40\text{ J}$$

hints: Once the pushing force is removed, the only force acting along the slope is the component of weight down the slope: $a = -g\sin 30^\circ = -5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
The block starts from $Q$ with speed $u = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ up the plane and returns to $P$, so the displacement is $s = -10\text{ m}$.
Set up the equation $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$: $-10 = 8t - 2.5t^2$, and solve the quadratic equation for the positive root.
walkthrough:
Calculate the acceleration down the slope after the pushing force is removed:
$$-mg\sin 30^\circ = ma \implies a = -g\sin 30^\circ = -10(0.5) = -5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Set up the displacement equation with initial velocity $u = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ up the slope and net displacement $s = -10\text{ m}$ (returning to $P$):
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$
$$-10 = 8t + \frac{1}{2}(-5)t^2$$
$$-10 = 8t - 2.5t^2$$

Rearrange into standard quadratic form and solve for $t$:
$$2.5t^2 - 8t - 10 = 0$$
Multiply through by $2$:
$$5t^2 - 16t - 20 = 0$$
$$t = \frac{16 \pm \sqrt{(-16)^2 - 4(5)(-20)}}{2(5)} = \frac{16 + \sqrt{256 + 400}}{10} = \frac{16 + \sqrt{656}}{10} \approx 4.16\text{ s}$$
teacher_walkthrough: After the pushing force is removed at point $Q$, the only force acting along the line of greatest slope is the component of gravity pulling downhill.

Apply Newton's second law along the slope, choosing the uphill direction as positive:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$-mg\sin 30^\circ = ma$$
Divide by $m$:
$$a = -g\sin 30^\circ = -10 \times 0.5 = -5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The block starts at $Q$ with an initial upward velocity of $u = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$. It momentarily comes to rest higher up the slope and then slides back down to $P$.

Since $P$ is $10\text{ m}$ downhill from $Q$, the total displacement is:
$$s = -10\text{ m}$$

Rearrange into standard quadratic form:
$$2.5t^2 - 8t - 10 = 0$$
Multiply every term by $2$ to obtain integer coefficients:
$$5t^2 - 16t - 20 = 0$$

Apply the quadratic formula with $a = 5$, $b = -16$, and $c = -20$:
$$t = \frac{-(-16) \pm \sqrt{(-16)^2 - 4(5)(-20)}}{2(5)}$$
$$t = \frac{16 \pm \sqrt{256 + 400}}{10} = \frac{16 \pm \sqrt{656}}{10}$$
Evaluate the square root:
$$\sqrt{656} \approx 25.6125$$
$$t = \frac{16 + 25.6125}{10} = \frac{41.6125}{10} \approx 4.16\text{ s}$$
